analysis.title: Investor Positioning and Flows: A Modest Bounce (13 November 2026)
key_insights: Aggregate equity positioning rose modestly to the 26th percentile (-0.35 sd) but is still well underweight. It recovered only slightly from last week's plunge. The S&P 500 bounced and is trying to return to the tight range held since August, but remains slightly below it.

Systematic strategies are at the 37th percentile (-0.06 sd), the lowest in 7 months, and kept cutting on weaker trend signals and higher vol. Cuts were largest in the Nasdaq 100, small caps and EM equities.

Discretionary positioning rebounded off the bottom of its band but is still deeply underweight at the 13th percentile (-0.60 sd). DB says the weakness goes beyond the resurgence in rates vol and is now disconnected from fundamental drivers such as macro data surprises.

US macro data surprises (CESI) are at the 95th percentile since 2003, the strongest since 2023. Then data kept defying recession forecasts. Now data is beating already robust expectations. DB argues this makes the discretionary underweight look excessive relative to fundamentals.
The MOVE index (1m, inverted) has a -62% correlation with large-cap discretionary positioning since 2021, so the resurgence in rates vol has weighed on discretionary equity exposure.

AAII sentiment (bull minus bear) is at the 8th percentile since 1987. Bullish responses are at the 26th percentile (eight-week low), bearish at the 96th percentile (eight-week high) and neutral at the 4th.

DB's sentiment-extreme study is stated two ways. The front-page summary says that after similar lows S&P 500 returns were mixed over one week but positive over one month 66% of the time with a median of +3%. The chart page shows a 1-week median of -0.4% (positive 47% of the time) and a 1-month median of 2.8% (positive 68%).

Tech positioning bounced to the 26th percentile (-0.09 sd) from its biggest underweight in 3.5 years, but the MCG and Tech ratio to the rest of the S&P 500 is still slightly below its long-run trend channel (trend growth 14.2% annualised, band +/-10%). DB remains overweight Tech after upgrading it on Oct 30 2026.

Sector positioning: Energy jumped back to overweight (83rd percentile), Financials rose to slightly overweight (51st), Healthcare is at its biggest overweight in nine months (64th), and Utilities tumbled to an extreme underweight (1st percentile). Consumer Staples stays near the bottom of its range (9th).

CTAs cut their overall equity allocation to the 42nd percentile, the lowest in seven months. Their Nasdaq 100 position (14th percentile) flipped to net short for the first time in seven months. US small cap shorts grew (22nd percentile) and US large cap longs were pared (48th).

CTAs raised long US dollar positioning to the 95th percentile and trimmed copper longs (89th percentile) and oil longs (76th). Bond shorts were pared in all major regions and gold shorts were covered slightly (26th).

Vol-control funds raised their equity allocation after last week's sharp cut (35th percentile), but it is well below recent highs and their sensitivity to further selloffs eased. Risk parity cut equities (70th percentile) while keeping commodity exposure extremely high (99th).

Equity fund inflows of $98.3bn were the largest in five months. The US took $63.6bn, EM $14.7bn (lowest in five weeks), broad global funds $14.5bn, Japan $4.2bn and Europe $0.4bn after four straight weeks of outflows. Within EM, Taiwan took $5.8bn, Korea $4.0bn and China $2.1bn.

Tech sector funds took in $8.9bn, a seventh straight week of inflows. Healthcare ($0.9bn) also had a seventh week of inflows. Energy (-$1.1bn), Utilities (-$0.8bn), Industrials (-$0.7bn) and Telecom (-$0.3bn) had outflows.

Bond fund flows fell sharply to their lowest since Liberation Day (Apr 2025). The report gives $11.6bn in the front-page summary and the weekly bullet but $0.3bn in the weekly summary line, an internal inconsistency. Broad-mandate funds (-$2.1bn) had outflows for the first time in nearly eight months, government bonds (-$0.6bn) and EM bonds (-$1.5bn) had outflows, and IG took $2.9bn.
Money market funds had outflows of $17.9bn after massive inflows the prior week. US funds saw -$24.2bn and Europe took in $6.0bn.

Options: the 5-day call-to-put volume ratio fell to the 48th percentile as net call volume dropped sharply in index options. S&P 500 3m 90-110 skew fell after a seven-month high last week. The basket of highest-net-call-volume stocks modestly outperformed this week.
DB S&P 500 forecasts: 2026 target 8000, 2026 EPS $362, 2027 EPS $430.

sector_views.rationale: DB upgraded Tech back to overweight on Oct 30 and remains overweight. Positioning recovered modestly but is still low at the 26th percentile and relative performance sits slightly below the long-run trend channel.

macro_indicators.reading: 95th percentile since 2003, at the top of its long-run range
macro_indicators.interpretation: Data is beating already robust expectations. DB says the last comparable surprise was in 2023, and discretionary positioning is far below what this reading has historically implied.
DB's S&P 500 target, with 2026 EPS of $362 and 2027 EPS of $430.

risk_factors: Resurgent rates vol, which has a -62% correlation with discretionary positioning since 2021.
Systematic strategies still cutting equity exposure on weaker trend signals and higher vol, especially in the Nasdaq 100, small caps and EM.
Discretionary positioning is deeply underweight and disconnected from macro data surprises, so it could stay low if the disconnect persists.
Tech relative performance is still slightly below its long-run trend channel after last week's plunge in Tech positioning.
The S&P 500 is still slightly below the tight range held since August.
Mixed one-week returns after previous sentiment extremes: median -0.4%, positive 47% of the time.
charts_described: Figure 1 plots equity positioning with systematic at the 37th percentile, discretionary at the 13th and overall at the 26th, percentiles since 2010.
Figure 2 plots US CESI against large-cap discretionary positioning, with a 2010-2019 correlation of 34%, showing positioning well below the level implied by surprises.
Figure 3 plots US CESI with a +/-75 band and a current percentile of 95% since 2003, with the 2023 recession-defying surprise period marked as the last comparable high.
Figure 4 plots the inverted 1m MOVE index against large-cap discretionary equity positioning, with a -62% correlation since 2021.
Figure 6 shows S&P 500 median returns after AAII spread lows (episodes since 2010): 1 month median 2.8% positive 68% of the time, 1 week median -0.4% positive 47% of the time.
Figure 7 plots the MCG and Tech ratio to the rest of the S&P 500 against a trend growing 14.2% annualised with a +/-10% band.
vol_and_positioning: Aggregate equity positioning is -0.35 sd (26th percentile), with discretionary at 13th percentile and systematic at 37th percentile.
Systematic strategies' positioning is at a 7-month low. Systematic positioning has a -77% correlation with S&P 500 1m realized vol, so higher vol drives further cuts.

CTA Nasdaq 100 positioning is at the 14th percentile and net short for the first time in seven months. CTA US small cap shorts are at the 22nd percentile and US large cap longs at the 48th. Japan is at the 26th percentile, Europe 60th and EM short positioning 34th.
Vol-control funds are at the 35th percentile equity allocation after a sharp cut the prior week. Risk parity equity weight is at the 70th percentile.
AAII bull-bear spread is at the 8th percentile since 1987, the bottom of a 4-decade range.
Call-to-put volume ratio (5d ma) is at the 48th percentile. S&P 500 3m 90-110 skew declined after a seven-month high last week.
Large-cap mutual fund beta to the S&P 500 is at the 25th percentile (1m rolling) and 22nd (3m rolling). Equity L/S hedge fund beta is at the 56th (1m) and 64th (3m) percentile.
Futures positioning data is as of Nov 3, one week older than the other series.

tension_points.bull_case: Macro data surprises are at the 95th percentile and beating robust expectations, sentiment is at the 8th percentile, and equity fund inflows hit a five-month high of $98.3bn. Past sentiment lows were followed by positive S&P 500 returns over the next month (66% to 68% of the time, median +3% or 2.8%). Discretionary positioning at the 13th percentile leaves room to add.
tension_points.bear_case: Systematic strategies are still cutting on weaker trend signals and higher vol, CTAs flipped net short the Nasdaq 100, and rates vol has a -62% correlation with discretionary positioning. One-week returns after prior sentiment lows were mixed (median -0.4%, positive 47% of the time).

tension_points.bull_case: DB is overweight Tech after the Oct 30 upgrade. Positioning recovered to the 26th percentile from the lowest in 3.5 years, relative performance is slightly below its long-run trend channel, and Tech funds took $8.9bn, a seventh straight week.
tension_points.bear_case: Tech positioning is still low, CTA Nasdaq 100 positioning (14th percentile) flipped net short and systematic cuts were largest in the Nasdaq 100. DB cut Tech to neutral on Oct 9 before moving back to overweight.
